Saudi Arabia. A vast, desert-dominated kingdom occupying most of the Arabian Peninsula in western Asia, home to Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and the planet's second-largest proven oil reserves. Founded in 1932 through the consolidation of tribal territories by Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud, the state derives its legitimacy from Wahhabist Islam and its wealth from petroleum exports, making it a dominant regional power and vital global actor despite its modest population. The kingdom's influence on Islamic theology, regional geopolitics, and world energy markets far exceeds its size.

Saudi Arabia occupies the central and eastern portions of the Arabian Peninsula, bordered by Jordan, Iraq, and Kuwait to the north, the Persian Gulf and Qatar to the east, the United Arab Emirates and Oman to the southeast, and the Red Sea to the west. The vast Rub' al-Khali, the Empty Quarter, one of the world's largest sand deserts, covers much of the southern interior. The landscape is predominantly arid, with mountainous regions along the Red Sea coast.

Mecca, in western Saudi Arabia, is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad around 570 CE and Islam's holiest site. Muslims are religiously obligated to perform the Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, at least once in their lifetime. Medina, Saudi Arabia's second-holiest city, is where Muhammad established the first Islamic community and mosque. It became the spiritual and administrative center of early Islam.

Saudi Arabia's oil reserves were discovered in 1938. The kingdom became the world's leading petroleum exporter in the mid-twentieth century and founded OPEC, the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries, in 1960 to control global oil prices. King Abdulaziz Ibn Saud, reigning from 1932 to 1953, unified the Arabian Peninsula through military conquest and political alliances, establishing the absolute monarchy that persists today under the House of Saud.

The kingdom's official religious ideology is Wahhabism, a puritanical Islamic reformation originating in eighteenth-century Arabia. It has influenced Islamic movements globally and defines Saudi Arabia's domestic and foreign policy. Saudi Arabia remains a critical American ally in the Middle East, though its human-rights record, strict religious governance, and regional interventions, especially in Yemen and against Iran, remain internationally controversial.
